observations.text: SP maintained the inbound and outbound course only under IP direction, with the IP flying part of the outbound leg after station passage. Radial deviation reached 11 degrees before any correction was initiated. Performance meets the block MIF of 0 but remains marginal for the Training Section. Chair-flying of the wind correction angle required immediately after station passage is expected to reduce the dependence on IP direction.

SP maintained the inbound course to the station and re-established the outbound radial after station passage, requiring only verbal prompts from the IP and no control input from him. Radial deviation was held at 8 degrees and was corrected once the prompt was given. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP tracked the course inbound and outbound without IP intervention and recognized the drift after station passage on his own initiative. Radial deviation did not exceed 7 degrees and was corrected in a timely manner with an appropriate wind correction angle. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed inbound and outbound tracking timely and accurately, re-establishing the selected course immediately after station passage. Radial deviation was contained within 4 degrees throughout the exercise, with the Basic A/C Control criteria maintained. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP set the wind correction angle before the drift became apparent and maintained the selected course both inbound and immediately after station passage. Radial deviation remained within 2 degrees for the entire exercise, with no prompting from the IP at any point. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a wind correction angle applied in the direction of the drift instead of into the wind, did not re-establish the outbound radial after station passage and the divergence continued to increase. Radial deviation reached 12 degrees, beyond the 8 degree limit, with the result that the IP directed the heading corrections and flew part of the outbound leg.

SP, due to an interrupted instrument cross-check while attention remained on the navigation display, did not monitor the CDI during the outbound leg and left the aircraft tracking away from the selected radial. Radial deviation reached 13 degrees before recognition, with the result that the IP took control to return the aircraft to the assigned course. The Basic A/C Control criteria were not maintained during the correction.

SP maintained inbound and outbound course within the block MIF of 1, re-establishing the radial after each of the IP's verbal prompts. Radial deviation twice reached 8 degrees and was recognized and corrected with delay. Marginal performance for the Training Section; a more disciplined cross-check between the CDI and the bearing pointer is expected to reduce the dependence on prompting.

SP tracked the course inbound and outbound and recognized the drift after station passage without any prompting from the IP. Radial deviation reached 6 degrees on the outbound leg and was corrected in a timely manner with a suitable wind correction angle. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed inbound and outbound tracking timely and accurately, holding the CDI centered through station passage and re-establishing the outbound radial without delay. Radial deviation did not exceed 4 degrees at any point of the exercise. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP established the wind correction angle before the drift developed and maintained the selected course throughout the exercise, including immediately after station passage. Radial deviation remained within 2 degrees, with heading, altitude and airspeed held to the same precision under the Basic A/C Control criteria. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to omitting re-identification of the station and confirmation of the OBS course setting before proceeding outbound, tracked a radial other than the one assigned and did not correct the divergence. Radial deviation reached 15 degrees from the assigned course, with the result that the IP set the correct course and directed the re-intercept.

SP, due to poor workload distribution, with navigation, communication and aircraft control attempted simultaneously, did not maintain the inbound course while copying the clearance and did not detect the divergence before station passage. Radial deviation reached 11 degrees, beyond the 8 degree limit, with the result that the IP took control to return the aircraft to the assigned radial.

SP, due to an insufficient wind correction angle carried over from the intercept, did not arrest the drift off the outbound radial and flew the leg with a constant divergence. Radial deviation reached 8 degrees and was recognized and corrected only after the IP's verbal prompt. No IP control input was required.

SP, due to distraction by a secondary cockpit task during the outbound leg, did not sustain the instrument cross-check on the CDI and allowed the course to drift after station passage. Radial deviation reached the 8 degree limit and was corrected with delay, following the IP's verbal prompt. Inbound tracking to the station was maintained without assistance.

SP maintained inbound and outbound tracking within the desired standards, applying the wind correction angle without IP intervention. Radial deviation reached 6 degrees on two occasions, both immediately after station passage, and was recognized and corrected in a timely manner. Marginal performance for this stage; earlier anticipation of the drift at station passage is expected to keep the deviations inside 5 degrees.

SP executed inbound and outbound tracking timely and flawlessly, holding the CDI centered and re-establishing the course immediately after station passage. Radial deviation did not exceed 3 degrees at any point, with the Basic A/C Control criteria maintained throughout. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP anticipated the drift and set the wind correction angle before station passage, so the outbound radial was held from the first moments of the outbound leg. Radial deviation remained within 2 degrees for the entire exercise, with no prompting from the IP. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to reversed interpretation of the CDI while tracking outbound, applied heading corrections away from the selected radial and did not arrest the resulting divergence. Radial deviation reached 14 degrees, well beyond the 8 degree limit, with the result that the IP took control and re-established the assigned course.

SP, due to attention captured by a minor system indication while the aircraft state went unmonitored, did not maintain the inbound course and did not identify station passage at the expected time. Radial deviation reached 12 degrees and heading control degraded beyond the Basic A/C Control criteria, with the result that the IP directed the recovery and flew the re-intercept.

SP, due to over-controlling in bank while chasing the CDI needle, did not stabilize a tracking heading either inbound or outbound and repeatedly overshot the selected radial. Radial deviation reached 8 degrees on each swing and was corrected only after the IP's verbal prompt to set and hold a wind correction angle. Recognition of the error was delayed on both occasions.

SP, due to an error that went undetected because the cross-check was not re-established after the frequency change, did not verify the selected course and tracked outbound with a steadily increasing divergence. Radial deviation reached the 8 degree limit before the IP's verbal prompt led to recognition and correction. Inbound tracking prior to the frequency change was maintained without assistance.

SP, due to a wind correction angle that was set late after station passage, did not hold the outbound radial during the first portion of the leg. Radial deviation reached 7 degrees, was recognized without prompting and was corrected in a timely manner with no IP intervention. Inbound tracking to the station remained within the desired standards.

SP, due to an incomplete mental model of the outbound sequence that was not updated when the clearance changed, did not set the new course promptly and continued briefly on the previous radial. Radial deviation reached 6 degrees before the error was self-detected, and the aircraft was returned to the assigned course in a timely manner without IP intervention.

SP executed inbound and outbound tracking within the desired standards, applying the wind correction angle without IP prompting. Radial deviation was contained within 5 degrees, reaching that value twice immediately after station passage. Marginal performance for this stage of training; tighter control of the correction at station passage is expected to keep the deviation inside 3 degrees.

SP maintained the selected course inbound and outbound with the wind correction angle established before any drift became apparent, including immediately after station passage. Radial deviation remained within 1 degree throughout, with altitude and airspeed held to the Basic A/C Control criteria at the same precision. Above end of block MIF achieved.
